content.title: Moon shot: NASA’s Artemis Space Launch System vs the Apollo Saturn V by the numbers
content.text: NewsApollo 17 vs Artemis 1 (NASA photos)The Space Launch System (SLS) NASA is planning to launch Monday is the biggest rocket capable of carrying humans since the Saturn V Apollo moon rocket. Development of both deep space rockets was led by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Ala. Here’s how the two compare by the numbers:Read More: Monday’s Artemis moon launch attempt means eyes on AlabamaHeight: Saturn V 363 feet; SLS 322 feet (23 stories)Weight at liftoff: Saturn V 6.2 million pounds; SLS 5.7 million poundsDiameter: Saturn V 33 feet;, SLS 27.6 feetEngines: Saturn V: Five F-1 engines; SLS: 4 RS-25 engines and two, five-segment solid-rocket boostersPower (thrust): Saturn V 7.5 million pounds; SLS 8.8 million poundsLift capability: Saturn V 100,000 pounds to the moon; SLS 154,000 pounds to the moonThe capsule: The Orion capsule atop SLS can hold four crew members compared to the Apollo capsule’s three. It has the familiar cone shape as previous capsules, but inside are what NASA says are “advances in life support, avionics, power systems, and advanced manufacturing techniques.”Successful launches: Saturn V 13 (12 for Apollo missions, one to place Skylab space station in orbit) SLS 0 (so far)Key point to remember: SLS relies on solid-fuel rocket boosters attached at the sides unlike Saturn V, which had a single stack propulsion system.Note: Artemis is designed to not only reach the moon for the first time with women and persons of color, but also eventually go to Mars.Lee Roop is a journalist with more than four decades experience reporting and leading reporting on Huntsville, Alabama's technical, military and scientific sectors.
